hook.text: Remember 4-9-2-8-3-7-1-5-6. Hard. Now try 492-837-156. Same digits, three chunks, much easier.

buildup.text: Chunking groups individual items into larger units, compressing information to fit working memory.

discovery.text: George Miller's magic number: working memory holds about four chunks, not four individual items.

twist.text: Expert chess players don't remember pieces—they remember board patterns. Chunks grow with expertise.

climax.text: Reading, language, music—every skill uses chunking. Mastery means building bigger chunks.

quiz.question: What does chunking do for working memory?
options: It groups items into larger units to fit more in
It reduces all items to single digits
It eliminates the need for memory

details.summary: Chunking is the process of grouping individual pieces of information into larger meaningful units. A phone number remembered as three chunks instead of ten digits illustrates the power of chunking. Experts in any domain use chunking to dramatically expand their effective working memory.
details.whyItMatters: Working memory is severely limited to about four items. Chunking is the primary mechanism by which expertise overcomes this fundamental cognitive bottleneck.
takeaways: Chunking groups individual items into meaningful clusters
It dramatically expands effective working memory capacity
Expert performance relies heavily on domain-specific chunking

faq.question: How many chunks can working memory hold?
faq.answer: Current research suggests about four chunks, revised down from Miller's famous seven plus or minus two. However, each chunk can contain many items. An expert chess player's chunk might contain an entire board position. The chunk limit is fixed, but chunk size grows with expertise.

faq.question: How do experts develop better chunks?
faq.answer: Through deliberate practice and experience. A beginner musician reads one note at a time. An expert sees entire phrases as single chunks. Medical students learn to chunk symptoms into diagnostic patterns. This chunking develops automatically through extensive, meaningful engagement with the domain.
